name: Pest Lead Agent · Book new lead

parameters.content:
## Pest Lead Agent: book a new lead

Fictional company (Ridgeway Pest Control), mocked vendor APIs. A new lead comes in; a qualified HubSpot deal, proposed FieldRoutes slots, a CSR task and a Slack alert go out. **Nothing is ever sent to a customer**: email is a Gmail draft, SMS is only a proposal in the CSR task.

**Config** comes from env: *_BASE_URL and tokens for HubSpot, ClickUp, Slack, Gmail, Sheets, FieldRoutes and Anthropic, plus LEAD_WEBHOOK_SECRET, OPS_RULES_SHEET_ID and the Slack channels (SLACK_LEADS_CHANNEL, SLACK_ALERTS_CHANNEL: names for the mock, ids for a real workspace). **Rules** (service area, pricing, approval thresholds, and the HubSpot pipeline and stage ids, which a real portal generates) live in the "Ridgeway ops rules" sheet. **Privacy**: Slack, ClickUp and Sheets get ids, links, first name and ZIP only. **Retries**: 3 retries 5 seconds apart on every network call; every write sends Idempotency-Key = event id + node name (stable across retries and redeliveries) and X-Run-Id = execution id. Failures of required steps go to "Pest Lead Agent · Alert on errors".

Signed webhook (HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp.rawBody, timing-safe, 300 s replay window), three sources normalized, E.164 phones, one claim per event_id in the event ledger. Bad or stale signature: 401. Invalid payload: 400. Event still in flight: 409 with Retry-After. Duplicate: 200. All four exit early with no side effects.

Claude (haiku 5.5) via raw HTTP with a JSON-schema output. The output is never trusted: guardrails re-validate every field and remove echoed phone numbers and emails. Invalid output or confidence below the sheet threshold goes to needs_review.

The service-area table is read from the ops rules sheet, like every other rule. ZIP to branch (Jacksonville, Savannah, Mobile). needs_review and out_of_area leads skip the customer check and the deal.

nodes.name: Receive lead
nodes.notes: Production webhook POST /webhook/ridgeway/lead. Keeps the raw body for the signature check.

nodes.name: Verify signature
nodes.notes: HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp.rawBody, timing-safe. Rejects a timestamp older than 300 s or over 60 s ahead, and a missing body. Sets the clock (fixed only in test mode).

nodes.name: Check signature result
nodes.notes: Early exit: a bad or missing signature ends the run here with no side effects.

nodes.name: Respond 401 unauthorized
nodes.notes: Answers 401. No vendor was called.

nodes.name: Normalize and validate lead
nodes.notes: Maps web_form, call_tracking and hubspot_form to one lead. Phones to E.164. Needs a phone or an email.

nodes.name: Check lead is valid
nodes.notes: Early exit: an unusable payload ends the run here.

nodes.name: Respond 400 invalid
nodes.notes: Answers 400 with the validation errors. No vendor was called.

nodes.name: Prepare event claim
nodes.notes: Builds the claim for the event ledger: the event id and this execution id.

nodes.name: Claim event
nodes.notes: Asks the event ledger for the claim on this event id. Critical: 3 retries 5 seconds apart, then the error workflow.

nodes.name: Check event claim
nodes.notes: Reads the ledger answer: claimed, in_flight (another run holds the event) or done. Anything else fails the run.

nodes.name: Route claim result
nodes.notes: Early exit: claimed continues; in_flight answers 409 with Retry-After; done answers 200 duplicate.

nodes.name: Respond 409 in flight
nodes.notes: Answers 409 {status: in_flight} with a Retry-After header. The sender tries again later. No vendor was called.

nodes.name: Respond duplicate
nodes.notes: Answers 200 {status: duplicate}. No vendor was called.

nodes.name: Fetch ops settings
nodes.notes: Reads the "Settings" tab: confidence threshold, urgency windows, approval rules and multipliers. Rules live in the sheet.

nodes.name: Prepare Claude request
nodes.notes: Parses the settings, then builds the request from workflow/anthropic.js: only inquiry text, source and ZIP leave the building.

nodes.name: Qualify lead with Claude
nodes.notes: Raw HTTP to ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/v1/messages with a JSON-schema output. Failure is non-critical: the next step routes it to review.

nodes.name: Apply AI guardrails
nodes.notes: Re-validates every model field against the allowlists and removes phone numbers and emails the model echoed. Bad output or low confidence (threshold from the sheet) means needs_review.

nodes.name: Fetch service area rules
nodes.notes: Reads the "Service area" tab of the Ridgeway ops rules sheet (values.get). Rules live in the sheet, not here.

nodes.name: Check service area
nodes.notes: ZIP to branch. Chooses the path: qualified, needs_review or out_of_area.

nodes.name: Route lead by path
nodes.notes: Qualified leads go to the customer check; the other two skip straight to the HubSpot contact.

parameters.content: FieldRoutes customer search by phone (email if no phone). An active customer is handled as a service request on their account instead of a new deal.

nodes.name: Prepare FieldRoutes customer search
nodes.notes: Query by phone, or email when there is no phone.

nodes.name: Find FieldRoutes customer
nodes.notes: FieldRoutes customer search. Failure is non-critical: treated as a new customer with a warning.

nodes.name: Check for existing customer
nodes.notes: An active FieldRoutes customer turns the lead into a service request.

nodes.name: Branch on existing customer
nodes.notes: Existing customers skip the deal and go to a CSR task.

parameters.content: Existing customer: a ClickUp CSR task and a Slack note. No new HubSpot deal.

nodes.name: Prepare ClickUp service request task
nodes.notes: Task for the CSR. First name, ZIP and ids only.

nodes.name: Create ClickUp service request task
nodes.notes: Creates the task. Idempotency-Key makes a retry harmless.

nodes.name: Prepare Slack service request alert
nodes.notes: Short note with the FieldRoutes customer id and the task id.

nodes.name: Post Slack service request alert
nodes.notes: Posts to #leads. Non-critical.

parameters.content: One search matches email OR phone (email wins), then update or create. A create refused because the email exists (the search lagged) reads that contact by email and updates it. Out-of-area leads are tagged, needs-review leads carry their status. The customer's original message is stored on the contact, so other systems only need the id.

nodes.name: Prepare HubSpot contact search
nodes.notes: One search matches email OR phone.

nodes.name: Search HubSpot contact
nodes.notes: HubSpot CRM v3 contact search. Critical: 3 retries 5 seconds apart, then the error workflow.

nodes.name: Prepare HubSpot contact upsert
nodes.notes: Picks the match (email wins) and builds the create or update properties, including the original message.

nodes.name: Branch on contact match
nodes.notes: Existing contact is updated, otherwise created.

nodes.name: Update HubSpot contact
nodes.notes: PATCH the contact (a search match, or the existing contact a refused create pointed to). Idempotency-Key per event and node.

nodes.name: Create HubSpot contact
nodes.notes: POST a new contact. Idempotency-Key per event and node (HubSpot ignores it). Its error output goes on: an email that already exists is refused.

nodes.name: Check HubSpot contact create
nodes.notes: A new contact id goes on. A refused create with an email (it already exists; search lagged) reads that contact; without an email it fails the run.

nodes.name: Branch on contact create
nodes.notes: Refused create: read the existing contact by email, then update it.

nodes.name: Find HubSpot contact by email
nodes.notes: GET the contact by its email (idProperty=email). 404 is an answer here, not an error.

nodes.name: Prepare contact update after conflict
nodes.notes: Found: update that contact with this lead. Not found: fail the run with both answers.

nodes.name: Record HubSpot contact
nodes.notes: Keeps the contact id for every later step.

nodes.name: Route lead after contact
nodes.notes: qualified continues to the deal; needs_review and out_of_area take their short branches.

nodes.name: 7. Needs review and out of area

parameters.content: needs_review: ClickUp review task and Slack, no deal, no slot. out_of_area: the contact is already tagged, so a short Slack note is all that is left.

nodes.name: Prepare Slack out-of-area note
nodes.notes: Short note: ZIP and the HubSpot contact link.

nodes.name: Post Slack out-of-area note
nodes.notes: Posts to #leads. Non-critical.

nodes.name: Prepare ClickUp review task
nodes.notes: Review task for a human; the original message is on the HubSpot contact.

nodes.name: Create ClickUp review task
nodes.notes: Creates the review task. Idempotency-Key makes a retry harmless.

nodes.name: Prepare Slack review alert
nodes.notes: Short note with the reason and the task id.

nodes.name: Post Slack review alert
nodes.notes: Posts to #leads. Non-critical.

parameters.content: Pricing and approval rules come from the ops rules sheet. A redelivery reads the deal by its unique ridgeway_event_id (GET with idProperty, not a search) instead of creating a second one; a create that conflicts on that property reads it too. The deal is created in "New lead" and associated to the contact. The FieldRoutes spot search covers the urgency window; a failure after 3 retries means no slots, a callback task and a Slack warning, and the run continues. The approval pest types, commercial properties (when the sheet says so) and a high value move the deal to "Needs approval".

nodes.name: Fetch pricing rules
nodes.notes: Reads the "Pricing" tab of the ops rules sheet.

nodes.name: Prepare HubSpot deal
nodes.notes: Picks the Pricing row (a termite letter request is priced as a WDO letter), estimates the value, decides on approval, builds the deal lookup.

nodes.name: Find HubSpot deal
nodes.notes: GET the deal by ridgeway_event_id (a unique-value property), not a search, which can lag. HubSpot ignores Idempotency-Key. 404 is an answer here.

nodes.name: Pick HubSpot deal
nodes.notes: Reuses the deal of an earlier attempt of this event (404: none, prepare the create). 429 or 5xx fails the run.

nodes.name: Branch on deal match
nodes.notes: A deal already exists for this event: skip the create.

nodes.name: Create HubSpot deal
nodes.notes: Deal in the New lead stage (pipeline and stage ids from the sheet), with ridgeway_event_id. Its error output goes on: a second create conflicts.

nodes.name: Record HubSpot deal
nodes.notes: Keeps the new deal id, or marks a refused create to be checked.

nodes.name: Branch on deal create
nodes.notes: Refused create: read the deal by ridgeway_event_id; it may exist from an attempt whose answer was lost.

nodes.name: Find HubSpot deal after conflict
nodes.notes: GET the deal by ridgeway_event_id after a refused create.

nodes.name: Reuse HubSpot deal after conflict
nodes.notes: Found: reuse it (warning hubspot_deal_create_conflict). Not found: fail the run with both answers.

nodes.name: Associate deal with contact
nodes.notes: HubSpot v4 default association, deal to contact.

nodes.name: Prepare FieldRoutes availability search
nodes.notes: Window by urgency in the branch time zone; the days per urgency come from the rules sheet.

nodes.name: Search FieldRoutes availability
nodes.notes: FieldRoutes spot search. Failure is non-critical: no slots, callback task, Slack warning.

nodes.name: Pick slots
nodes.notes: Up to 3 open slots inside the window and at least an hour from now.

nodes.name: Branch on availability
nodes.notes: If the search failed, create a callback task and warn Slack; the run continues.

nodes.name: Prepare callback task
nodes.notes: Call-back-to-book task for the CSR.

nodes.name: Create ClickUp callback task
nodes.notes: Creates the task. Idempotency-Key makes a retry harmless.

nodes.name: Prepare FieldRoutes warning
nodes.notes: Slack warning text.

nodes.name: Post Slack FieldRoutes warning
nodes.notes: Posts to #leads. Non-critical.

nodes.name: Prepare deal stage update
nodes.notes: Records the final stage the deal should have.

nodes.name: Branch on approval
nodes.notes: Approval pest types, commercial (when the sheet says so) or a value over the threshold need approval. A reused deal that already moved on keeps its stage.

nodes.name: Move deal to Needs approval
nodes.notes: PATCH the deal stage. Idempotency-Key per run.

parameters.content: Gmail draft only, never sent. SMS is proposed only when consent normalizes to true (boolean true, or the form strings true, yes, checked or on); otherwise the reason is recorded. The ClickUp CSR task carries ids, links, slots and the proposed SMS; Slack #leads gets the summary, with Approve and Hold buttons when approval is required.

nodes.name: Prepare Gmail draft
nodes.notes: Drafts the customer email (never sent) and proposes an SMS only with explicit consent.

nodes.name: Branch on email
nodes.notes: No email address means no draft.

nodes.name: Create Gmail draft
nodes.notes: Creates a draft only. Non-critical: a failure shows up in the CSR task and as a gmail_draft_failed warning.

nodes.name: Prepare ClickUp CSR task
nodes.notes: Full handoff for the CSR: ids, links, slots, proposed SMS, the custom fields, and whether the Gmail draft exists.

nodes.name: Create ClickUp CSR task
nodes.notes: Creates the task. Idempotency-Key makes a retry harmless.

nodes.name: Prepare Slack leads summary
nodes.notes: Block Kit summary; Approve and Hold buttons (value: the event id only) when approval is required.

nodes.name: Post Slack leads summary
nodes.notes: Posts to #leads. Non-critical.

parameters.content: Every path ends here: append received_at, finished_at and status to the Google Sheets log, tell the event ledger the event is done (so a redelivery answers duplicate), respond 200 with the result.

nodes.name: Compose result
nodes.notes: Every path ends here: builds the response and the log row.

nodes.name: Append speed-to-lead row
nodes.notes: One row per lead: ids, timestamps, status. No personal data. Non-critical.

nodes.name: Prepare event done
nodes.notes: Builds the done request: status plus the ids later steps look up by event id (deal, CSR task, Slack message).

nodes.name: Mark event done
nodes.notes: Tells the ledger the event is finished (a redelivery answers duplicate) and stores the ids for Approve / Hold. Non-critical.

nodes.name: Respond with result
nodes.notes: Answers 200 with the result.
